name: Essential Upsell & Cross Sell
summary: Shopify upsell and cross-sell app with frequently-bought-together blocks, product-page and cart-drawer offers, one-click post-purchase upsells, bundles, add-ons and automatic discounts, with plans tiered by the extra revenue the app attributes to its offers.
best_for: Shopify stores that want product-page, cart and post-purchase upsells, frequently-bought-together blocks and add-ons in one app, with a monthly plan that rises in steps as the offers sell, from free up to $149.99 a month in the app on 16 Nov 2026
skip_if: you want cart-drawer upsells for free, since cart-page offers start on the $19.99 Essential plan; you will not grant an app access to customer and order data; or you only want post-purchase offers and would rather pay a share of upsell revenue than a fixed plan
honest_knock:
The plans are metered on revenue the app says it generated, and the free plan's $100 a month is a small allowance. A store whose upsells work moves up the ladder because they work: $500 on Starter, $1,000 on Essential, $2,500 on Growth at $39.99 a month, and further steps up to Unlimited at $149.99 a month above $10,000. The vendor's pricing page (read 22 Nov 2026) now says how that revenue is counted: the value of products bought through an offer once the order completes, not the product the shopper was already buying. Passing a limit moves the store up a plan by itself, and a store on Free that passes $100 lands on a paid plan without a trial, so one good month on the free plan can start a bill. Enterprise is quoted individually.

Cart offers start on Essential at $19.99. On 2 Oct 2026 the vendor's own page also listed them on Starter; on 22 Nov 2026 the listing and the vendor's page both put them on Essential. The cart drawer is where many stores want an upsell, so a store that wants it there starts at $19.99, not $9.99.

The free plan is a real plan, but it does not look like one at install. A US merchant wrote in February 2026 that the app advertised a free plan and then pushed a free trial; the vendor replied that the free plan has a revenue limit and needs a Shopify approval step. Read the approval screen rather than closing it.

The app asks for a lot of data. The listing says it needs to view and edit customers, products, orders, discounts and the online store. Two US merchants dropped it to one star in 2024 and 2025 over permissions that covered customers' personal details and recent orders; the vendor answered that the access is for the performance analytics merchants asked for. If you keep a tight data policy, read the permission screen before you approve it.

The rest of the criticism is about fit with a theme or a store setup. A French merchant uninstalled in November 2025 because widgets did not show on pages whose product handle had been translated; the vendor replied in February 2026 that product targeting now uses the product ID instead of the handle. A UK merchant wrote in September 2025 that it did not work with their cart drawer. The positive reviews mostly praise support that fixed this kind of clash, such as a merchant in Romania whose cart offers broke the item list on a Halo theme and were fixed within a day in September 2026. We installed it in a Shopify development store on 16 Nov 2026.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · per month for up to $500 of revenue generated by the app
pricing.notes: (read 2 Oct 2026 on the Shopify listing and the vendor's own page; read again on 16 Nov 2026 together with the plan screen in the app, and on 22 Nov 2026 on the listing and on the vendor's pricing page at essential-apps.com/upsell/pricing-info) Plans are priced not on orders or views but on the extra revenue the app generates in a month. Free covers up to $100 of generated revenue with product-page and post-purchase offers, analytics and translations. Starter is $9.99 a month for up to $500. Essential is $19.99 a month for up to $1,000 and is the first plan with cart-page offers. Growth is $39.99 a month for up to $2,500. Above that, the vendor's pricing page and the plan screen in the app list Scale at $59.99 for up to $5,000, Professional at $99.99 for up to $10,000 and Unlimited at $149.99 above $10,000, plus Enterprise, priced on a call; the Shopify listing shows only Free to Growth. On 2 Oct 2026 we had read Professional as $39.99 with no revenue limit; that no longer matches. A paid plan starts with a 14-day free trial when you choose your first paid plan yourself, once per store. The vendor's pricing page, read 22 Nov 2026, says added revenue is the value of products shoppers add and buy through your offers once the order is completed, and that the product a shopper was already buying does not count. Passing a limit moves the store to the next plan automatically, and a store on Free that passes $100 is moved to a paid plan without the free trial. Paid plans carry a 30-day money-back guarantee, claimed through support. Stores that were already on a plan when this pricing launched keep their plan and price. On 2 Oct 2026 the vendor's page also listed cart offers on Starter; on 22 Nov 2026 it puts them on Essential, as the listing does. All charges are in USD, billed through Shopify every 30 days. Developer Essential Bundles & Upsells, with an address in Vilnius, Lithuania; the listing gives a launch date of 10 June 2024 and showed 2,511 reviews at 5.0 on 22 Nov 2026.

compare_with.name: AfterSell
compare_with.why: AfterSell is the closest app in our own dossiers, and the two price on different things. On our reading of 27 September 2026, AfterSell charged by monthly order volume: its Post-Purchase plan started at $34.99 a month for 200 orders and its Pre-Purchase and Complete plans at $59.99 and $79.99, with each rising as orders grow. Essential Upsell & Cross Sell prices on the extra revenue it generates instead: free up to $100, then $9.99, $19.99 and a $39.99 Growth plan for up to $2,500 of generated revenue, with higher steps up to $149.99 a month in the app on 16 Nov 2026. The plans from Essential up cover product-page, cart and post-purchase offers together. A store with many orders and modest upsell revenue will usually pay less with Essential; AfterSell's own pages are worth reading if you want its checkout-focused offers.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Essential Upsell and Cross Sell on the development store plan: a post-purchase offer, publishing it, a test checkout with the test gateway, the offer after payment, the pricing plans and the uninstall dialog. The offer was declined and nothing was paid or uninstalled. Create offer opens Choose placement type: Product page, Cart page, Pop-up, Post purchase page and Suggest new placement type; Post purchase page was chosen. A yellow bar said that the Essential Upsell app is not activated yet and to click Activate and choose Essential Upsell as the post-purchase app in Shopify, then click Save. An info block lists cases where the post-purchase funnel does not appear: payments requiring CVN, installment plans, missing shipping details and orders under $0.50. The tabs are Content, Offer and Design. Offer: trigger All products, First offer Specific products with The Compare at Price Snowboard ($785.95, compare at $885.95), Discount type No discount and Shipping type Free shipping. Save gave Offer created successfully. and Publish gave Updated successfully. Activate opened Shopify Settings, Checkout, Use an app to add features at checkout after payment, with the choices None, Essential Upsell and Post Purchase Upsell Hero; it stood on Post Purchase Upsell Hero from another test. We chose Essential Upsell and saved (Changes saved.); the funnel of the other app was not touched. A test order through the theme preview (no store password): The Complete Snowboard at $699.95, Buy it now, a made up address and the test gateway with card number 1. After Pay now the page showed an exclusive offer, a countdown Hurry! This exclusive deal expires in: 14:58, The Compare at Price Snowboard at $785.95 with $885.95 struck through, Pay Now and Decline offer. Although the offer was set to No discount, it showed a lower price, because $885.95 is the compare at price of the product. Decline led straight to the thank you page with the $699.95 order. The app dashboard afterwards showed Impressions 1, Conversions 0, Conversion Rate 0.00% and Added revenue $0.00, and the Setup Guide 1 / 3 completed. Timing, approximate tester observations: Install at 15:04:45 and the offer in view at about 15:08:10, about 3 minutes 25 seconds and about 17 steps (install 2, creating and publishing the offer 8, activating 3, ordering 4). The Settings, Apps row has a menu with Open app, View details, Get support and Uninstall; the Uninstall dialog (reason list, feedback box) was opened and cancelled. Not tested: product page, cart page and pop-up offers, the app embed in the theme, paying for the offer, the paid plans and the 14-day trial, the cart drawer placement and real conversion. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: An offer set to No discount still showed a price cut, because the product compare at price was struck through, and the setting for the post-purchase app in Shopify had to be switched from another app first.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Essential Upsell and Cross Sell on the development store plan: a post-purchase offer, publishing it, a test checkout with the test gateway, the offer after payment, the pricing plans and the uninstall dialog. The offer was declined and nothing was paid or uninstalled. Create offer opens Choose placement type: Product page, Cart page, Pop-up, Post purchase page and Suggest new placement type; Post purchase page was chosen. A yellow bar said that the Essential Upsell app is not activated yet and to click Activate and choose Essential Upsell as the post-purchase app in Shopify, then click Save. An info block lists cases where the post-purchase funnel does not appear: payments requiring CVN, installment plans, missing shipping details and orders under $0.50. The tabs are Content, Offer and Design. Offer: trigger All products, First offer Specific products with The Compare at Price Snowboard ($785.95, compare at $885.95), Discount type No discount and Shipping type Free shipping. Save gave Offer created successfully. and Publish gave Updated successfully. Activate opened Shopify Settings, Checkout, Use an app to add features at checkout after payment, with the choices None, Essential Upsell and Post Purchase Upsell Hero; it stood on Post Purchase Upsell Hero from another test. We chose Essential Upsell and saved (Changes saved.); the funnel of the other app was not touched. A test order through the theme preview (no store password): The Complete Snowboard at $699.95, Buy it now, a made up address and the test gateway with card number 1. After Pay now the page showed an exclusive offer, a countdown Hurry! This exclusive deal expires in: 14:58, The Compare at Price Snowboard at $785.95 with $885.95 struck through, Pay Now and Decline offer. Although the offer was set to No discount, it showed a lower price, because $885.95 is the compare at price of the product. Decline led straight to the thank you page with the $699.95 order. The app dashboard afterwards showed Impressions 1, Conversions 0, Conversion Rate 0.00% and Added revenue $0.00, and the Setup Guide 1 / 3 completed. Timing, approximate tester observations: Install at 15:04:45 and the offer in view at about 15:08:10, about 3 minutes 25 seconds and about 17 steps (install 2, creating and publishing the offer 8, activating 3, ordering 4). The Settings, Apps row has a menu with Open app, View details, Get support and Uninstall; the Uninstall dialog (reason list, feedback box) was opened and cancelled. Not tested: product page, cart page and pop-up offers, the app embed in the theme, paying for the offer, the paid plans and the 14-day trial, the cart drawer placement and real conversion. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: An offer set to No discount still showed a price cut, because the product compare at price was struck through, and the setting for the post-purchase app in Shopify had to be switched from another app first.

Session and source-reading date: 16 November 2026. Times are CET. The session started at about 15:04 CET. These are approximate tester observations, not benchmark timings. Midnight timestamps are required date anchors, not measured event times.
